speech.transcript: Cryptography hides meaning. Stegenography hides the message itself. The attacker does not even know a message exists. Unlike cryptography, it does not scramble the message. It just makes the message invisible. Stegonography is the art and science of hiding the existence of communication. A message is concealed inside another medium. An image, an audio clip, a text file, or even a network protocol. Adversaries cannot detect it. Cryptography conceals content. Stegenography conceals existence. An encrypted text looks random. A stego image looks like an ordinary image. The two goals are different, and they are often used together. Linguistic Stegonography A null cipher hides words inside a harmless sentence. A grill reveals selected letters through a mask. Micro dots shrink a whole page into a tiny dot. The secret hides in the wording itself. Technical Stegenography Invisible Ink on paper Tiny characters behind white spaces Physical tricks, not algorithms These are the oldest methods Digital Stegonography Least significant bit embedding changes the last bits of image pixels. Spread spectrum spreads the signal across a wide band. Spam can carry hidden text. The secret hides in the noise. Cryptography says, read this if you can. Stegenography says, there is nothing to read. Together they give both secrecy and stealth. That is the difference.
